mechanical_architecture: An audacious feat of subterranean engineering cutting straight through the granite root of the central mountain range. Twin heavy bronze rail lines run fifteen miles down a continuous twelve-degree incline, linking high alpine mining redoubts directly to lowland smelter valleys. Heavy descending ore trains haul ascending passenger gondolas via a five-mile counterbalanced steel-and-hemp cable system. * The Incline Head (Upper Station): A fortified timber-and-iron terminus perched on an alpine ledge. Giant grooved sheave wheels twelve feet in diameter regulate descending velocity using manual water-cooled friction shoes. * The Dark Run: Carriages plunge into a narrow, unlit granite bore. Hand lanterns illuminate rushing rock walls mere inches from passengers' shoulders as air pressure pops ears during the two-thousand-foot drop.

four_corners.establishment: The Caldera Transit Company & Sulfur Guild - Tough, ash-covered engineers who inspect shoe soles and sell vinegar-soaked breath masks. They charge heavy tolls in exchange for guided transit between geyser cycles.
four_corners.opponent: The Fire-Born Zealots - Hermits who worship the subterranean magma pulse. They wedge timber logs into the vent-chimneys to build up pressure and explode causeway sections beneath foreign invaders.
four_corners.shadow: The Black-Powder Chemical Syndicate - Greedy arms merchants who force indentured laborers to harvest sulfur inside boiling fumaroles without breathing masks to maximize explosive yields.
four_corners.outcast: The Ash-Stalker Smugglers - Outcasts wearing thick cork-soled boots and leather respirators. They know the safe wading shallows across the boiling acid flats when the main causeway is closed by guards.

overview: High-Temperature Volcanic Transit, Industrial Sulfur Crust, Pumice Stone
mechanical_architecture: An ancient, natural hexagonal columnar basalt formation paved over with iron slag and volcanic mortar. The causeway stretches three miles directly across a steaming caldera basin and a boiling turquoise sulfur lake, cutting through an otherwise impassable ring of smoking volcanic craters. * The Hexagonal Roadbed: Columns of basalt packed tight as giant cobblestones, naturally resisting high geothermal temperatures while radiating intense ground heat. * The Vent-Chimney Pylons: Iron pipes driven deep into fissures along the causeway edge, venting pressurized steam safely eighty feet above the roadway to prevent roadbed explosions. * The Sulfur Scrape Stations: Fortified huts equipped with long scrapers and zinc buckets where miners harvest pure yellow sulfur crust cooling along the water's edge.
